# NSR field mapping: CCT DataBridge to OpenG2P NSR household intake

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-nsr-mapping-doc.js from server/integrations/nsr/mapping.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Source of truth: `server/integrations/nsr/mapping.json` (machine-readable; the mapper interprets it, tests check it against the specification). Specification: `docs/architecture/CCT_DataBridge_NSR_Webhook_Specification.md` v1.1. Canonical schema: `prototype/schema.js` (145 fields, from `NSR_Registry_Build_Sheet.xlsx` > Create Fields, whose *NSR source* column names the NSR form field for each canonical field).

## Summary

- The specification names **121 household fields** (sections 1-7) and **81 fields per member** (section 8): 202 in all. DataBridge holds **145** canonical fields. They are not one-to-one.
- Classification of the 202 specification fields: DIRECT 20, ALIAS 11, TRANSFORMED 92, DERIVED 41, MISSING 2, REVIEW_REQUIRED 36.
- 21 canonical fields have no NSR field and are not sent (listed at the end).
- Rule: **a key is sent only when DataBridge holds a value for it.** No defaults are filled in, and missing answers are never turned into "NO".
- Consent is always sent and must be `true` on every member record; otherwise the household is blocked (`CONSENT_NOT_GIVEN` / `CONSENT_MISSING`).

Classifications:

- **DIRECT**: Same meaning and value format; sent under the NSR key.
- **ALIAS**: The spec lists the DataBridge key as an accepted alias; sent under the NSR key.
- **TRANSFORMED**: Value converted to the documented NSR value.
- **DERIVED**: Computed from DataBridge values without inventing data.
- **MISSING**: DataBridge does not collect this; never sent.
- **REVIEW_REQUIRED**: Needs confirmation from the NSR team (value vocabulary, meaning or format).

## Household grouping

DataBridge stores one record per person, with household values repeated on each. The mapper builds one NSR household from all records sharing an `nsr_household_serial`:

- **Head**: the record with `is_household_head = true` or `relationship_to_head = "1"`. None, more than one, or the two fields disagreeing blocks the household (`NO_HEAD`, `MULTIPLE_HEADS`, `HEAD_CONFLICT`).
- **Household values** (every field whose build-sheet object is *Household*) are taken once. If members carry different values the household is blocked (`HOUSEHOLD_FIELD_CONFLICT`); DataBridge never picks one. In the seeded demo data this blocks 9 of 13 households, because the synthetic generator gives members of one household different addresses and dwelling values.
- **`member_count`** must equal the number of member records (`MEMBER_COUNT_MISMATCH`), so `total_heads` always matches `household_members`.
- **Duplicates**: two records with the same NIN, or the same name and birth date, block the household (`DUPLICATE_MEMBER`).
- **Order**: head first, then by `internal_record_id`, so the same records always produce the same payload.
- **Limits**: more than `NSR_WEBHOOK_MAX_MEMBERS` (default 50) members blocks the household (`TOO_MANY_MEMBERS`); nothing is truncated.
- The stored records are never changed. The household `content_hash` is computed from the source records (not the payload, whose `age` changes with the date) and drives duplicate-submission protection.

Columns: target NSR field; DataBridge source; keys the NSR template accepts (from the specification); transformation; DataBridge data type; NSR default when the key is absent (from the specification); whether the source exists; whether it is derived; whether more source data is needed; classification; notes.

## Source fields DataBridge does not have

These specification fields are never sent. Fields marked REVIEW_REQUIRED here need a decision, not just data.

- `unlisted_enum` (1. Survey and consent): **MISSING**. The build sheet merges enumerator and unlisted enumerator into enumerator_id.
- `disroster` (2. Composition and headship): **REVIEW_REQUIRED**. Meaning not documented and no build-sheet field. Not sent, so NSR records "YES".
- `connin` (8. Household members roster (per member)): **REVIEW_REQUIRED**. Confirmation (re-entry) field on the paper/ODK form. DataBridge holds one value only and does not copy it into the confirmation field. Confirm with the NSR team whether it is required.
- `contrackid` (8. Household members roster (per member)): **REVIEW_REQUIRED**. Confirmation (re-entry) field on the paper/ODK form. DataBridge holds one value only and does not copy it into the confirmation field. Confirm with the NSR team whether it is required.
- `confrim_contactno` (8. Household members roster (per member)): **REVIEW_REQUIRED**. Confirmation (re-entry) field on the paper/ODK form. DataBridge holds one value only and does not copy it into the confirmation field. Confirm with the NSR team whether it is required. The key is spelled "confrim" in the spec.
- `caccountno` (8. Household members roster (per member)): **REVIEW_REQUIRED**. Confirmation (re-entry) field on the paper/ODK form. DataBridge holds one value only and does not copy it into the confirmation field. Confirm with the NSR team whether it is required.
- `cbvn` (8. Household members roster (per member)): **REVIEW_REQUIRED**. Confirmation (re-entry) field on the paper/ODK form. DataBridge holds one value only and does not copy it into the confirmation field. Confirm with the NSR team whether it is required.
- `health_problem_label` (8. Household members roster (per member)): **MISSING**. No build-sheet field. Possibly a form label rather than data: confirm.

## Where the specification's defaults conflict with DataBridge data

The NSR template fills a default for an absent key. DataBridge never sends a value it does not hold, so for these fields the NSR record can show something DataBridge never collected. The preview lists each case as a `NSR_DEFAULT_APPLIES` warning.

| NSR field | NSR default | Effect when DataBridge has no value |
|---|---|---|
| `sponsor` | `"FEDERAL_GOVERNMENT"` | Build-sheet sponsors (UNICEF, GIZ, NG CARES, State, AfDB, WFP, Others) do not match the NSR list. Mapped provisionally: State -> STATE_GOVERNMENT, Others -> OTHER, the rest -> DEVELOPMENT_PARTNER (NG CARES is federal, World Bank financed: confirm). If absent, NSR records FEDERAL_GOVERNMENT. |
| `consent` | `"YES"` | Never reached: consent is always sent, and the household is blocked without it. |
| `enumerator` | `"CCT_DATABRIDGE"` | coordinate_source is deliberately NOT sent: NSR would read it ("NSR field enumeration") as the enumerator name. If enumerator_id is absent, NSR records "CCT_DATABRIDGE". |
| `community` | `"Community"` | Mandatory in DataBridge, so the NSR default is not reached. |
| `gps` | `"0.0 0.0 0.0 0.0"` | Sent as latitude, longitude, accuracy_m for NSR to format. DataBridge has no altitude, so it does not build the "lat lon alt acc" string itself. If coordinates are absent, NSR records "0.0 0.0 0.0 0.0" (a real point at sea): confirm NSR can leave it empty. |
| `total_heads` | `1` | Must equal the number of member records grouped under the household, or the household is blocked. |
| `disroster` | `"YES"` | Meaning not documented and no build-sheet field. Not sent, so NSR records "YES". |
| `roof_dwelling` | `"1"` | Build-sheet roof label (Code Lists tab). The spec default "1" is a code, but NSR shows the value as received. |
| `num_room` | `1` | NSR records the default. |
| `anyshocks` | `"NO"` | If absent, NSR records "NO". |
| `health_insurance` | `"NO"` | Code 2 ("Don't know") has no NSR value and is not sent, so NSR records "NO": confirm whether NSR accepts an unknown value. |
| `hh_crops_options` | `"NO"` | NSR records "NO" for every crop and other_crop, although the crops were never asked. |

**Question for the NSR team:** can the template leave an absent key empty instead of applying these defaults? Until then, households without these values reach NSR with defaults DataBridge did not collect.

|---|---|

| `country_code` | Always NG; no NSR field. |
| `data_source` | DataBridge lineage field. |
| `synthetic` | No NSR field. NSR cannot tell test data from real data: see the open questions. |
| `household_name` | Derived display name; NSR builds its own. |
| `zone_id` | No NSR field. |
| `zone_name` | No NSR field. |
| `state_id` | No NSR field (state_name is sent). |
| `lga_id` | No NSR field (lga_name is sent). |
| `rural_urban` | No NSR field in the specification. |
| `coordinate_source` | Deliberately not sent: the spec lists it as an alias for enumerator. |
| `coordinate_verified` | No NSR field. |
| `administrative_level` | No NSR field. |
| `code_system` | No NSR field. |
| `geo_lowest_level_value_id` | No NSR field. |
| `geo_code_hierarchy_json` | No NSR field. |
| `monthly_income` | No NSR field in the specification. |
| `birth_date_estimated` | No NSR field; see the "day" mapping. |
| `email` | No NSR field in the specification. |
| `nsr_number` | No NSR field in the specification. |
